#### #75 sunbiz-depth (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: Sunbiz's public SFTP (sftp.floridados.gov, user Public / password <published-password>, both published in plaintext on dos.fl.gov) is live and updated daily, and holds far more than the daily corporate file already scouted 08/02: Fictitious Name filings+events (with an explicit COUNTY field, verified populated "LEE"/"COLLIER"), Federal Tax Lien data split into 4 files (filings/events/debtors/secured-parties, city+ZIP fields, verified Naples/Fort Myers/Cape Coral debtor rows), General Partnership filings+events, and Trademark/Mark filings. A Quarterly full-state snapshot (cordata.zip, corevent.zip, plus quarterly fic/gen/lien/mark zips) runs Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct. Judgment liens and annual reports are confirmed NOT available as bulk files anywhere on Sunbiz — both are e-file-only transactions (verified on two separate pages, and the daily/quarterly download pages explicitly state annual reports "are not considered events and are not included in the downloads"). Best leading-indicator candidate is the fictitious-name (DBA) filings feed: a new sole-proprietor/DBA registration in Lee/Collier is a raw small-business-formation signal, one step earlier than a business license or a first invoice, and is free, county-tagged, and updated on every business day. Run 2: The Sunbiz SFTP (sftp.floridados.gov, user Public / password <published-password>, both public and confirmed live) hosts far more than the daily corporate file already scouted 08/02: fictitious name filings+events, federal tax lien filings/events/debtors/secured-parties, general partnership, and trademark data, each as daily deltas AND as quarterly full-population zips. All have fixed-width layouts with published field definitions and real county/city/ZIP columns; live pulls returned actual Lee County (North Fort Myers 33903) and Collier County (Naples 34104/34109) rows, so SWFL is directly filterable. Annual reports are NOT a separate download — they're 3 report-date fields already embedded in the corporate record layout, so nothing new to build there. Judgment liens are a genuine dead end for bulk purposes: filed with Sunbiz but distributed only via a one-name-at-a-time web search (jlilist.html / jlidet.html), no bulk file or API found in 3 fetches. New-entity registration itself (fic/cor/gen filings) is the leading-indicator candidate here: a name filed today precedes any license, permit, deed, or lease by weeks to months.

### Wealth & unobvious signals

#### #76 faa-aircraft-registry (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: Verified live and downloaded the full FAA Releasable Aircraft Database (registry.faa.gov/database/ReleasableAircraft.zip, 73MB actual vs ~60MB stated). It unpacks to MASTER.txt (current registrations, 316,993 rows, comma-delimited with header) plus ACFTREF (aircraft model reference for joining to get type/category incl. jets), DEALER, DEREG (deregistered aircraft), DOCINDEX, ENGINE, and RESERVED. MASTER.txt carries a COUNTY field that is a bare 3-digit FIPS county code (no state prefix) alongside STATE, so filtering to Lee (071), Collier (021), Hendry (051) with STATE=FL is a clean county join. Counted 731 Lee, 511 Collier, 127 Hendry rows (1,369 total) of currently-registered aircraft with a registrant address in-county. TYPE AIRCRAFT and MFR MDL CODE fields let you join to ACFTREF to classify jets vs. props/helicopters/gliders; that join wasn't run in this scout (out of scope) but the field exists and is populated. File is refreshed daily per the FAA page; no history/vintage snapshots are offered (this is a current-state file), so trend analysis over time requires our own daily/weekly pulls going forward — there is no bulk historical archive endpoint discovered. Not currently in our data holdings (ATTOM/FAA not held; this is a distinct free federal source). Run 2: The FAA Releasable Aircraft Database is a free, keyless, daily-updated 60MB ZIP (verified: actually 70MB compressed, ~535MB uncompressed across 8 files) containing every U.S. civil aircraft registration. MASTER.txt (317k rows nationwide) gives registrant name/address/city/state/ZIP/county-FIPS/status per N-number, with TYPE AIRCRAFT and TYPE ENGINE codes letting jets/turboprops be isolated. Verified live: Lee County (FIPS 071) has 731 registered aircraft (43 jets/turbofans), Collier (021) has 511 (75 jets), Hendry (051) has 127 (1 jet) — Naples (Collier) skews heavily toward jets (LLC-owned, consistent with high-net-worth second-home/seasonal-resident registrants). No sale price or true "purchase date" field, but CERT ISSUE DATE and LAST ACTION DATE approximate when a plane was newly registered to a local owner, which is the closest thing to a leading wealth-inflow signal here.

- **FAA Releasable Aircraft Database (MASTER.txt)** (Federal Aviation Administration, Civil Aviation Registry) — score 4/5, verified live by scout
  - Data URL: https://registry.faa.gov/database/ReleasableAircraft.zip

#### #77 opensky (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: OpenSky's REST API is verified live. Live current-position aircraft (`/states/all`) work fully anonymously (400 credits/day, ~1 sq° credit tiers) and returned two real aircraft over the SWFL bounding box in-session, with an aircraft `category` field (0-20 enum incl. Light/private-jet size classes) available via `extended=1` — but on the sampled call the field came back `0` (no info), meaning ADS-B category reporting is inconsistent for this use, not blocked. The specific ask — historical arrivals/departures by airport (`/flights/arrival`, `/flights/departure`) for KAPF/KRSW — is NOT available anonymously: live-tested and confirmed 403 "You cannot access historical flights." Since March 2026 OpenSky requires OAuth2 client-credentials (a free registered account, `client_id`/`client_secret`, 30-min bearer tokens) for every endpoint except `/states/own`; anonymous users get 400 credits/day per endpoint bucket (states/tracks/flights independent), authenticated standard users get 4,000/day, and flights/tracks queries cost far more credits than states queries (4 credits for live/<24h, scaling to 960×N for >25-day spans). No tail-number-level "private jet" flag exists in the data; you'd infer business/GA aviation from ICAO24/aircraft-type lookups or the `category` enum, which is not reliably populated. Full historical bulk access is only via a separate Trino/MinIO interface (also needs the same registered account), not scouted in depth here. Run 2: OpenSky's REST API is real and free, but historical arrivals/departures (`/flights/arrival`, `/flights/departure`) return a hard 403 "You cannot access historical flights" for anonymous callers — verified live against KAPF. Only the free OAuth2 client-credentials registration (client_id/client_secret from an OpenSky account) unlocks those endpoints; anonymous access is limited to live-only current-second state vectors over a bounding box (verified live over a SWFL box, 400 credits/day). Critically, neither the state-vector nor the flights schema carries aircraft type/model — identifying "private jet" traffic requires joining icao24 to a separate aircraft metadata database, and the metadata download URL I tried (opensky-network.org/data/data) 404'd, so that join path is unverified. Terms of use also cap the API to "research and non-commercial purposes," which is a real friction point for a commercial product like SWFL Data Gulf.

#### #78 uscg-vessels (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: The official USCG "Merchant Vessels of the United States" file (dco.uscg.mil) is confirmed to exist, is free, monthly, and per its own page description includes hailing port plus "managing owner identification information" — but the actual .zip/.pdf downloads on dco.uscg.mil sit behind an Akamai block that returned 403 to every curl and crawl4ai attempt in this session (same shape as the known LandMarkWeb dead end), so it is not verified_live. A third-party GitHub mirror (msquaremarinesolutions-create/boat-names-dataset) republishes the identical monthly USCG extract as a plain CSV with no bot-wall; I fetched it live (36.7MB, 395,728 rows) and confirmed real Lee/Collier rows: 1,102 valid documented Naples FL vessels, 510 Fort Myers, 680 Cape Coral, 468 Marco Island — including a 130.9ft yacht (FANDANGLE, built 2022) hailing from Naples and 29 vessels 80ft+ across the four ports. This mirror carries no owner name/address at all (deliberately stripped), so it only proves hailing-port density, not ownership — it's a single snapshot (as of 2026-08-05), not a time series, so no month-over-month trend claim is supported yet. Whether the raw official file still contains owner city/state/ZIP (as opposed to full street address, which was removed in 2017) is unverified and would be the more valuable wealth signal than hailing port (which is just what's painted on the transom, owner's choice). PSIX (the other named surface) has no hailing-port, city, or owner field in any of its documented SOAP outputs — it's a vessel-ID lookup service for inspection/case history, not a bulk ownership-by-location database. Run 2: USCG's public vessel-lookup surfaces (PSIX web UI at cgmix.uscg.mil/PSIX and its underlying PSIXData.asmx XML/SOAP service) are real, free, keyless, and confirmed live, but they are single-vessel lookups by name/official number/HIN/call sign only — there is no city, hailing port, ZIP, or geography search field anywhere in the UI, the XLSX export tool, or the SOAP API's documented parameters, and no bulk file/dataset download exists. Verified directly against a real vessel record (detail postback returned Name/VIN/HIN/Flag/Service/Length/Breadth/Depth/Build Year — no hailing port, no owner, no address). USCG's own DocumentationLink page states explicitly that vessel ownership on documented vessels is Privacy Act-protected and only available as a paid product from NVDC ($25 Abstract of Title / $125 Certificate of Ownership); the free NMFS lookup mirrors it once pointed to are dead (DNS failure on st.nmfs.gov). The PSIX XLSX Export tool is a different dataset entirely (Port State Control inspection/deficiency/MISLE incident data by USCG district, not vessel documentation or ownership). Net: this is a dead end for a free, bulk, location-filterable yacht/wealth signal for SWFL — the data that would make it useful (hailing port + owner location, filterable to Lee/Collier/Hendry) is either absent from the free surface or explicitly paywalled.

Confirmed by also testing an unrelated PDF on the same host/path pattern (Third Party Awareness 2024), also 403 — this is a path-wide bot block, not a one-file fluke.
  - NVDC/PSIX bulk data download or CSV/API by hailing port or city (https://cgmix.uscg.mil/PSIX/PSIXSearch.aspx): No such field or download exists. PSIX search fields (web UI, contact search, and SOAP API alike) are limited to Vessel Name, Primary Vessel Number, HIN, Call Sign, Flag, Service Type, and Build Year. Confirmed by crawling PSIXSearch.aspx, PSIXContactSearch.aspx, and the PSIXData.asmx method list, and by pulling one live vessel detail record via POST postback, which showed no hailing port, owner, or address field.
  - Vessel owner name/address on documented vessels (free) (http://cgmix.uscg.mil/PSIX/DocumentationLink.aspx): USCG's own page states this is Privacy Act-protected and sold only as a paid NVDC product (Abstract of Title $25/vessel, Certificate of Ownership $125/vessel) -- explicitly excluded by the no-paid-lanes rule.
  - NMFS free vessel-owner lookup mirrors (VesselByName.html / VesselByID.html) (https://www.st.nmfs.gov/st1/CoastGuard/VesselByName.html): Both URLs linked from USCG's own DocumentationLink page are dead: the host www.st.nmfs.gov fails to resolve (DNS error) in this session.

#### #79 black-marble (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: NASA Black Marble VNP46A3 (monthly) and VNP46A2 (daily) are real, live products at LAADS DAAC, gridded 15-arcsec HDF5 rasters starting 2012-01-01, in a 10°x10° tile scheme (Florida = tile h09v06, unverified exact tile but math checks out from the 36x18 grid). LAADS's own JSON listing API (`/api/v2/content/details/...`) is fully keyless and returns real per-tile filenames, sizes (~130MB/tile) and timestamps — so file discovery and freshness checks need zero auth. Actually pulling pixel data requires a free NASA Earthdata Login (URS) token: an anonymous HEAD/byte-range request to the archive silently 200s but serves an HTML login page instead of HDF5 bytes (verified with a 1KB range request — got `<!DOCTYPE html>` not HDF5 magic bytes). The commonly-cited "no login needed" mirror, EOG/Colorado School of Mines (eogdata.mines.edu), now also requires free account registration (confirmed: their v22 annual directory renders a Keycloak sign-in wall via JS, not a public dosettings.tif.gz link). No keyless, no-download, pre-aggregated county-level Black Marble series was found anywhere in this pass — this is a raster product with no county rollup service; any use requires either registering for Earthdata Login + downloading/clipping tiles (or using Google Earth Engine's Black Marble collection, out of scope here — GEE needs its own account), or NASA's AppEEARS point/area-extraction tool (also gated behind the same Earthdata Login, not tested this pass). Recommend: register one free Earthdata Login account (5-minute self-serve form, confirmed live) if this dataset is prioritized, then use AppEEARS or the LAADS API + h09v06 tile to build a monthly Lee/Collier average-radiance time series without hand-downloading full global tiles. Run 2: The Black Marble monthly/daily nighttime-lights products (VNP46A2/VNP46A3) are real and confirmed live on LAADS DAAC — 15 arc-second global grid, data from Jan 2012, GeoTIFF/HDF5 tiles with radiance + QA layers — but every download path is auth-gated: LAADS's own archive redirects unauthenticated requests straight to Earthdata Login (free registration, not one of our two API keys), and the long-assumed "keyless" EOG mines.edu mirror now also 302-redirects its monthly and annual directory listings to a Keycloak registration wall as of today, so that assumption is stale. I checked NASA's AppEEARS tool specifically because it can return pre-aggregated point/polygon time series without a raster download — its live 187-product catalog has no VNP46/nighttime-lights product at all, so that "avoid big rasters" path does not exist for Black Marble. The one genuinely keyless S3 bucket I found (source.coop `vnp46a1_thermal_anomaly`) is a NASA-Black-Marble-derived fire/gas-flare detection training set scoped to specific case-study tiles, not a general SWFL-covering radiance archive, so it doesn't satisfy the ask. Bottom line: the data exists and is real, but every practical path requires either a free Earthdata/EOG account plus r [...]

#### #80 wikipedia-pageviews (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: The Wikimedia Pageviews REST API is keyless, free, and live-verified for all 10 target SWFL place articles at monthly and daily granularity, back to 07/2015, current through at least 08/2025 (Naples). Every place tested (Naples, Fort Myers, Sanibel, Bonita Springs, Estero, Marco Island, Immokalee, Lehigh Acres, Ave Maria, Cape Coral) shows a real, repeating winter-peak / summer-trough seasonal curve — Naples 2019: Jan 32,203 views down to a Jun trough of 21,330 (about 34% lower), then back up in Dec to 26,164; the same shape recurs in 2025 (Jan 20,917 → Jun 13,835 → Jul/Aug rebound). This lines up with SWFL's snowbird season (peak Nov–Apr) and is a plausible free, near-real-time (monthly cadence, ~2-day lag per docs) proxy for seasonal visitor/interest intensity months before Q1 tax-season closings or seasonal-population-driven retail/permit data show up. One important caveat: the very first months of API history (Jul–Aug 2015) show wildly inflated then collapsing counts (e.g., Naples 25,222 → 763) — a known early-API/bot-filtering artifact — so any historical pull should start no earlier than ~2016 or apply the API's own bot-exclusion agent filter (already used: agent=user) and sanity-check the first few months. Run 2: Verified live: the Wikimedia REST Pageviews API (wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/metrics/pageviews/per-article) returns daily/monthly view counts, no auth, for all 10 assigned SWFL city articles, with history from 2015-07-01 through the present (partial current month). Pulled 10+ years of monthly data for Cape Coral and confirmed two real seasonality patterns: (1) a winter/snowbird baseline lift (January views routinely 20-70% above the Aug/Sep trough most years, e.g. Jan 2016 22,736 vs Aug 2016 12,415; Jan 2021 14,377 vs Sep 2021 10,703), and (2) massive, short-lived spikes tied to hurricane landfalls that swamp the seasonal signal — Sept 2017 (Irma) 34,810, Sept 2022 (Ian, made direct landfall on Cape Coral) 55,150 + Oct 2022 26,373, Oct 2024 (Milton) 29,963. This is a genuine, free, granular, long-history dataset we do not hold, and the hurricane-driven view spike is a plausible near-real-time (daily-lag) proxy for national attention to a specific SWFL place, ahead of slower official disaster/migration data.

#### #81 epa-echo-frs (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: EPA's ECHO REST API (echodata.epa.gov, no key) is live and returns real facility-level rows for Lee (7,295), Collier (2,830), and Hendry (661) counties FL, including name/address/lat-lon/RegistryID/NAICS-SIC(often null)/compliance status/last-inspection date/penalty history. It's a real, free, keyless, county-grain source we don't currently hold. The catch: it's a regulatory-compliance snapshot (RCRA/CWA/CAA/SDWA universe — pollution-permitted facilities), not a general business-formation registry, and the date fields that would make it a true "new registration" leading indicator (CREATE_DATE/UPDATE_DATE in the companion FRS Envirofacts table) came back null on the one row sampled, so the leading-indicator angle is unverified, not confirmed. Best fit as a slow-moving industrial/permitted-facility inventory layer, not a fast-moving activity signal, unless a date field is found populated on a wider sample. Run 2: EPA ECHO's echo_rest_services REST API is live, keyless, and filters cleanly to Lee (12071), Collier (12021), and Hendry (12051) via the p_fips parameter (county FIPS), confirmed with real row counts (7,073 / 2,736 / 592 regulated facilities respectively) and a sample facility record showing name, address, lat/long, NAICS/SIC placeholders, RegistryID, compliance status by program (CAA/CWA/RCRA/SDWA/TRI), inspection counts, and FacDateLastInspection. This is a facility-level regulatory/compliance signal (who's permitted, inspected, in violation) rather than a construction-permit or new-business-formation feed — its "new registration" angle is weak since the sample record's last inspection was 1988, meaning it's mostly a static/slow-moving compliance registry, not a fresh activity indicator. Full FRS bulk downloads and NAICS-code filtering for industrial/construction subsets were not verified live due to budget; that's the main gap for turning this into a leading indicator.

#### #82 fl-ucc (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: The Florida Secured Transaction Registry (floridaucc.com, run by vendor Image API LLC / FloridaUCC LLC for the Dept of State under Ch. 679 Fla. Stat.) has a real, free, keyless backing API at publicsearchapi.floridaucc.com (its own root path prints "Under Construction" but the actual endpoints work — verified live via its Swagger spec at /swagger/v1/swagger.json). It exposes a name/document-number Search endpoint plus a Downloads endpoint that hands back signed CloudFront URLs to pipe-delimited CSVs: daily incremental files (Debtors, Secureds, Filings, Events) for any given business day, and a full statewide snapshot (Full/Debtors ~196MB zip, last built 09/26/2026). Pulled 5 daily Debtors files (09/18-09/23/2026) and confirmed real rows for Fort Myers, North Fort Myers, Cape Coral, Naples and Estero with debtor name, address, city, state, ZIP and filing status — exactly the fields the assignment asked for. The Filings file carries FilingDate/FilingExpDate per UCC-1 number, and the daily debtor volume (~70-1,100 debtor rows/day statewide, no per-county breakout) means Lee/Collier rows are a real but modest slice, filterable client-side by ZIP/city after download. No county field exists — must filter by ZIP/city prefix ourselves. This is a genuine new-business-activity leading indicator (equipment/inventory financing precedes many small-business openings and expansions) and is entirely free/keyless, which is a strong fit for the four-lane sourcing model. Run 2: The Florida Secured Transaction Registry (floridaucc.com, operated by FloridaUCC LLC under contract to the FL Dept of State per Ch. 679) has a real, keyless, undocumented-but-public JSON API at publicsearchapi.floridaucc.com backing its React search UI. Two usable lanes verified live this session: (1) a name/company Search endpoint returning debtor name, UCC number, address, city, ZIP, state, status; (2) a Downloads endpoint that hands back a signed CloudFront URL to daily pipe-delimited CSV drops of that day's new Debtors/Secureds/Filings/Events (statewide, not county-filtered, ~2-3 days publish lag), plus "Full" ZIP snapshots of the whole registry (debtors_full.zip alone is ~196MB). Confirmed Lee/Collier debtor rows (Fort Myers, Naples, Cape Coral, Bonita Springs) in a freshly re-pulled daily CSV. No API key, login, or payment needed for either lane — it's the same backend the free public search page uses, just called directly. This duplicates none of our held sources (nothing in our list touches UCC/secured-lending filings) and is a genuinely new business-credit/investment-appetite signal, filterable to SWFL by DebZipCode/DebCity in the daily/full CSVs.

Run 2: All three verified live. Nonemployer Statistics (NES) confirmed at county x NAICS grain for Lee/Collier/Hendry, annual 2013-2023, via CENSUS_API_KEY. ZIP Business Patterns as a standalone "zbp" dataset is discontinued after the 2018 vintage (2019-2023 all 404); ZIP-level business counts moved into the CBP dataset itself (confirmed live for 2022, all-industry total only, no NAICS breakout) - this is the same CBP program we already hold at county grain, now also queryable at ZIP. Biggest find: county-level Business Formation Statistics NOW EXISTS as a public bulk XLSX (not via the EITS timeseries API, which still only supports "us" geography and 400s on state/county) - "Annual Business Applications by County," 2005-2025(partial), with real rows for Lee/Collier/Hendry counties. This overturns the 08/02/2026 dead end that said BFS was US/state grain only.

#### #84 economic-census (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: Both the 2022 Economic Census (ecnbasic) and the 2022 Annual Business Survey (abscs, absmcb) are live on the Census API with CENSUS_API_KEY and genuinely carry SWFL rows down to county and even city ("economic place") grain — this is new and NOT in our held inventory (CBP is county-only; this adds NAICS-detail establishment/receipts counts plus owner-demographic business characteristics). ecnbasic gave full NAICS-hierarchy detail (2-6 digit) with ESTAB/EMP/PAYANN/RCPTOT for Lee (071), Collier (021), Hendry (051), and city-level rows for Cape Coral and Naples. ABS company summary (abscs) gave firm/employment/payroll/receipts totals for all three counties; ABS business characteristics (absmcb) confirmed county-level owner demographic slicing (sex/ethnicity/race/veteran status) exists for Lee county, though a plain query without NAICS/characteristic filters collapses to one "Total" row — deeper cuts need explicit predicate values, which is a follow-up-build detail, not a scouting blocker. No paid lanes, no scrapes; everything came from keyless-shape JSON endpoints authenticated only with the existing CENSUS_API_KEY. Run 2: Both the 2022 Economic Census: Summary Statistics (ecnbasic) and the Annual Business Survey: Company Summary (abscs) are live on the Census API with a real CENSUS_API_KEY and both return county-level rows for Lee (12071) and Collier (12021); Hendry (12051) exists as a geography but returned zero rows for any NAICS breakout (too small/suppressed). ecnbasic also publishes true "economic place" tabulations for Cape Coral, Fort Myers, Naples city, and Marco Island (540/440/etc NAICS rows each), giving city-level establishment counts, employment and payroll by detailed NAICS — something our current sources (CBP, QCEW) only give at county grain. ABS additionally breaks county totals out by owner sex/ethnicity/race/veteran-group codes and is available for at least 2022 and 2023 vintages (annual cadence, not just quinquennial economic-census years), which is new relative to what we hold (CBP has no demographic-of-owner cut). Neither table overlaps our existing Census CBP/ACS/VIP holdings exactly since neither goes to city grain nor gives owner demographics.

#### #85 business-tax-receipts (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: No free, unattended-fetchable BTR dataset exists for any of the four assignment targets as of 09/26/2026. Lee TC (leetc.com) and Collier TC (colliertaxcollector.com) are brochure/FAQ sites with only PDF applications, no search or export. Both counties' actual BTR transaction system lives on Grant Street Group's county-taxes.com/county-taxes.net platform: it is a JS-rendered SPA that returns "Loading..." to a headless fetch, and per-receipt print pages (lee.county-taxes.com/public/business_tax/print_receipt?bt_receipt_id=N) are individually public but sit behind a Cloudflare managed-challenge (403, JS+cookie check) that blocks unattended scraping — a new, closely-related dead end to the existing "Lee Clerk LandMarkWeb" Cloudflare/Akamai block. Cape Coral's BTR intake runs through EnerGov Citizen Self-Service, which requires login before any record search is exposed. Fort Myers's Business-Tax page is an in-person/mail-only application with no online lookup, search, or data export; its Transparency Portal and OpenGov instance cover budget/financial data only, not BTR records. Net: this remains a real potential leading-indicator series (new-business formation by category/ZIP, ahead of employment and construction data) but is not currently reachable without either registration/paid access or a browser-automation approach beyond this scout's tools. Run 2: Both Lee and Collier County Tax Collectors route their "Request Real Estate, Tangible and Business Tax Reports" tool through the same third-party platform (Grant Street's county-taxes.com), and that platform is behind an active Cloudflare Turnstile challenge — confirmed blocked to both curl and headless crawl4ai (403 "Just a moment..." for both counties, identical infrastructure). Cape Coral and Fort Myers both run Tyler Technologies EnerGov Citizen Self-Service (CSS), which the client config confirms includes an anonymous "Public Information" (PageTitle_PublicSearch) module for looking up licenses/businesses without login — a real, non-obvious BTR lead — but the actual search grid is rendered client-side via Angular route changes and backing REST calls I could not resolve within this session's crawl4ai/curl toolset (two guessed API paths both 404'd cleanly, meaning the API exists but the correct resource path needs browser network-tab inspection, which is out of scope here). No BTR row-level data was retrieved from any of the four target sources this session; all four are leads/dead-ends, not verified-live datasets.

### Local government & public safety

#### #86 legistar-agendas (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: None of the six SWFL governments in scope run Legistar (webapi.legistar.com returned "LegistarConnectionString setting is not set up" for 14 guessed client slugs covering all six names — a clean, verified dead end for the whole assignment's stated hypothesis). Instead each uses a different vendor: Collier County BCC runs CivicClerk with a real, free, keyless OData REST API (colliercofl.api.civicclerk.com) exposing 1,646 meeting/event records with board name, date, category and agenda-file linkage — the one genuinely useful structured find here. Lee County BoCC uses NovusAGENDA (leecounty.novusagenda.com), Fort Myers uses CivicPlus AgendaCenter (agendas) plus Granicus (video only), and Bonita Springs/Naples/Cape Coral post agendas as PDFs on generic CivicPlus/Drupal CMS pages — all HTML/PDF only, no API. Item-level rezoning/matter text lives inside PDFs in every case, including Collier's API (agendaId links to a file, not structured fields), so none of these give machine-readable rezoning/approval data without PDF parsing. Run 2: None of the six target SWFL governments run Legistar — all 9 guessed client slugs (leegov, leecounty, colliercounty, capecoral, fortmyers, naples, bonitasprings, cityoffortmyers, naplesgov) hit a live but empty webapi.legistar.com endpoint that returned "LegistarConnectionString setting is not set up ... for client: X," and a DuckDuckGo search across all six found zero legistar.com hosts. The real landscape is fragmented: Lee BoCC and Collier BoCC both run CivicClerk, and CivicClerk exposes a genuine keyless OData JSON API (leecofl.api.civicclerk.com/v1/Events, colliercofl.api.civicclerk.com/v1/Events) giving meeting name/date/category and direct PDF links to the Agenda and Agenda Packet files — but not item-level rezoning text via the API itself (would need PDF parsing, a separate build). Fort Myers and Naples both run Granicus and expose classic keyless RSS "Agenda Feed" endpoints (ViewPublisherRSS.php) listing ~100 recent/upcoming meeting titles including Planning Advisory Board and Design Review Board (Naples) — the actual rezoning/development bodies. Cape Coral runs eSCRIBE (pub-capecoral.escribemeetings.com), confirmed live with a "Planning and Zoning Commission" meeting-type filter, HTML only. Bonita Springs' agenda page is on the city's own CivicPlus-style CMS (cms/One.aspx?portalId=); the actual packet/PDF listing wasn't captured in the crawl (nav chrome only) so it stays unverified.

#### #87 hearing-examiner (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: Collier County runs its Hearing Examiner and Planning Commission meetings on the CivicClerk platform, which exposes a live, keyless OData JSON API (colliercofl.api.civicclerk.com) listing every meeting/agenda by category with dates back to 2020 (HEX) and 2018 (Planning Commission), plus scheduled meetings out to 2027 — this is a genuine structured feed, not a scrape. Collier Clerk's separate legal-notices site (notices.collierclerk.com/genre/hearing-examiner/) publishes live individual HEX petition notices with PL-numbers, addresses and hearing dates, a good near-real-time companion feed. Lee County has no comparable API: its Hearing Examiner page routes to a legacy SharePoint search UI and a docsearch.leegov.com KwikTag portal that blocks scripted POST queries (503), but a related and independently reachable KwikTag instance (results.leegov.com) returns real, structured (GET, non-JS) zoning-case document listings keyed by case number (verified live with 20 real rows for case DCI2020-00010) — this is the closest thing Lee has to a structured case history, though it is document-index-shaped, not a case-metadata feed, and case numbers must be known/guessed rather than browsed. No Lee ArcGIS "Zoning Cases" REST/FeatureServer endpoint could be confirmed live within budget (the maps.leegov.com Hub landing page is JS-only and the dataset id/service URL was not found in the fetches run); flagging as unresolved rather than dead. Run 2: Collier County runs its Hearing Examiner (HEX) and Planning Commission (PC) on the CivicClerk platform, which exposes a live, keyless OData JSON API (colliercofl.api.civicclerk.com) listing every meeting/event back to 2018 (PC) and 2020 (HEX), including future-scheduled events through 2027 — verified live with real rows. This is a meeting-level history feed (date, category, agenda name/id), not an item-level list of individual variance/rezoning case numbers; getting to case-level detail (petition numbers, applicant, action) would require pulling each meeting's agenda-packet PDF, which the API's Events/Meetings entities don't expose as a direct field. Lee County has no equivalent structured feed: its "Zoning Hearing Calendar & Agendas" page is a JS-rendered CivicPlus events widget with no data visible in a static fetch, its Hearing Examiner decision search runs on SharePoint search behind a sign-in wall (the anonymous SP REST search call errored), and its DCD document-search portal only works as a per-known-case-number lookup (e.g., DCI2020-00010) returning that case's documents (HEX recommendation, staff report, BCC resolution, hearing recording) — useful for enrichment but not a browsable case list, and it sits behind Akamai bot protections per prior dead-end notes. Net: one real, live Collier source at meeting grain; Lee is a dead end for a list/feed.

#### #88 mpo-projects (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: Found one genuinely new, small, statewide ArcGIS REST layer (FDOT Active Construction Projects) with live Cost/StartDate/EstEndDate rows for Lee (13), Collier (14) and Hendry (2) — this is new, not our AADT or permit lanes, and it's a plausible near-term leading indicator for construction-driven local spending/labor demand. Lee MPO and Collier MPO both publish their TIPs as PDF-only downloads (no GIS/XLSX API); Collier's current FY2027-2031 TIP (adopted 06/12/2026, 19MB) and Lee's TIP bundle (150MB of PDFs) were both fetched and confirmed live but are PDF-table extraction projects, not clean API pulls. FDOT District 1's own "Active Projects" list is a small (80KB) PDF, statewide-district scope, confirmed to include Lee/Collier/Hendry roadway segments by name. A promising-looking "FDOT Five Year Work Program" ArcGIS layer and a "2024_2028 TIP Points" layer both turned out to be false leads (Tampa-Bay-only extent and Berkshire MPO Massachusetts, respectively) — flagged as dead ends. Run 2: Best hit is a live ArcGIS REST feature layer at gis.fdot.gov called "Active Construction Projects" (FDOT statewide, District 1 included) with per-project Cost, StartDate, EstEndDate, Vendor and County fields, verified with real Lee (13), Collier (14) and Hendry (2) rows. A second FDOT source, the D1 Contracts Office's own PDF "Active Projects - District One Construction," gives Contract ID/FinProj/cost-center but no cost or dates in the extracted text. Both Lee MPO and Collier MPO publish their TIPs only as PDFs (Lee: FY2027-2031 on leempo.com's document portal; Collier: FY2027-2031 PDF, 19MB, MPO-adopted 06/12/2026) with no XLSX or open API; neither has a GIS layer of TIP projects with cost/phase/schedule attributes despite ArcGIS items suggestively named "2024_2028_TIP_Points" and "Collier_MPO" — both turned out to be road-network/bike-ped GIS layers mislabeled or unrelated to the TIP project list, a genuine dead end worth flagging so nobody re-chases those URLs expecting project data.

#### #90 calls-for-service (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: Collier County Sheriff's Office publishes a genuinely structured, free, no-auth bulk CAD extract (crimedata.zip -> CrimeReportView.txt), refreshed every 3 hours, with per-call lat/lon, address, CAD event number, incident type, and disposition text; verified live with a fresh download containing ~1,264 rows spanning roughly the trailing 24 hours (09/24-09/25/2026 in the file I pulled). It has no built-in history, so value requires our own polling cadence to accumulate a time series. Lee County Sheriff's Office only offers a per-address "Incidents By Location" search (2.5 years of closed incidents) with no bulk export - useful for point lookups, not for a scan. Fort Myers PD and Naples PD route the public to third-party map-only products (crimemapping.com and a dead Flash-based CrimeMapper respectively) with no bulk data path found; Cape Coral PD's CityProtect widget is a JS SPA that returned no fetchable content within budget. Neither county's open-data/ArcGIS catalog (Lee GIS, Collier GIS Hub, Cape Coral ArcGIS Hub) carries a crime/police/CAD layer. Run 2: Collier County Sheriff's Office (CCSO) publishes a genuinely live, free, no-auth Calls-for-Service (CAD) feed as a tab-delimited text file, refreshed every 3 hours, verified with real Collier rows today (event #, address, incident type, timestamp, lat/lon). It has no depth of history though — it's a rolling window covering roughly the last day; we'd have to poll and archive it ourselves to build a time series. Lee County Sheriff's Office has no equivalent bulk feed: its "Incidents by Location" tool is address-search-only (no bulk export) and its "Crime Mapping" page is an empty JS widget shell with no identifiable underlying API. Cape Coral PD, Fort Myers PD, and Naples PD all route the public to closed vendor products (Cape Coral/others via CityProtect/Motorola Command Central SPA which returned a WAF "Request Rejected" on a direct fetch; Fort Myers via CrimeMapping.com/LexisNexis, also WAF-blocked on a keyless probe; Naples via a long-dead Flash-based "Crime Mapper" app) — none exposed a free bulk/API surface in this session. Cape Coral's and Collier County's ArcGIS open-data catalogs were checked directly and contain zero police/CAD/crime datasets (Collier's DCAT catalog is literally empty; Cape Coral's 77-dataset catalog has none titled police/crime/CAD/incident).

### Agriculture & rural lands

#### #91 nass-quickstats (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: The NASS Quick Stats REST API requires a free API key obtained by email registration (auth=free_key_missing, confirmed at quickstats.nass.usda.gov/api). But NASS also publishes the ENTIRE Quick Stats database as keyless, no-registration bulk .gz text files at nass.usda.gov/datasets, refreshed on weekdays. I range-fetched partial bytes of two of these (qs.census2022.txt.gz and today's qs.crops_20260926.txt.gz) and confirmed real rows for Lee (12071), Collier (12021) and Hendry (12051) FL counties, spanning CENSUS (every-5-year, 2002-2022) and SURVEY (annual, and some WEEKLY-cadence commodities) records, tab-delimited with COUNTY_ANSI/COUNTY_NAME/STATE_ALPHA fields to filter on. This is a real, previously-unscouted, free, county-grain agriculture dataset not currently in our lake. Full-file downloads (1.05GB crops, 295MB census2022) exceed the assignment's ~60MB single-file budget, so a real ingest would need the API key route (state_alpha=FL&county_code=071,021,051 filters keep responses small) or a streaming/chunked pull of the bulk files rather than a full download. Run 2: NASS QuickStats API requires a free-registration key we don't have (auth=free_key_missing), so live filtered pulls are blocked, but the API page itself confirms scope (county-grain, WHAT/WHERE/WHEN params, CSV/JSON/XML, 50K row cap). The keyless workaround exists and is real: NASS's bulk `.gz` dumps at nass.usda.gov/datasets/ are reachable with no key (HTTP 200, valid gzip) but are 46MB–1.05GB, over the per-fetch budget to fully pull. The practical keyless route is the 2022 Census of Agriculture Florida county-level text report (flv1.txt, 11.5MB, no auth) which I downloaded in full and confirmed has real Lee/Collier/Hendry rows across ~39 tables — farms count, land in farms (acres), land value, farm-size distribution, and commodity detail down to county level including citrus (Collier: 37 orange farms / 16,047 acres in one table) and sugarcane. This is a genuine, verified, free, county-grain dataset we do not currently hold, published every 5 years (2002/2007/2012/2017/2022, next due ~2027).

#### #92 ams-market-news (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: USDA AMS still runs the Immokalee-district vegetable price report daily and keyless, but as a PDF (not a structured feed) — it names Immokalee only as the weather-header location for a multi-county "SOUTH FLORIDA" price district, with no county/ZIP granularity. The structured/raw MyMarketNews (MMN) API that could give clean rows requires free registration and a personal API key we do not hold. A related national "Tomato Fax" weekly shipment-volume report is keyless too, but the current (off-season) week showed no domestic Florida-origin volume rows, only import border-crossing rows, so SWFL-specific volume coverage in that report is unverified either way this week. Net: one small, real, keyless PDF lane exists now (South Florida vegetable FOB prices incl. Immokalee as named district); the richer historical/volume data sits behind a free-but-unregistered key. Run 2: USDA AMS runs the Immokalee-district produce market through the Orlando (Oviedo, FL) Specialty Crops Market News office, and two of its daily reports are fully keyless, static PDFs updated every business day: OR_FV120 (shipping-point vegetable PRICES, names Immokalee/South Florida explicitly) and OR_FV170 (statewide FL truck/air/boat shipment MOVEMENT/VOLUME in 10,000-lb units and package counts). Both verified live today with real rows. The full structured historical time-series sits behind the MyMarketNews/MARS v1.2 API, which is free but requires eAuth account registration to get a personal API key (confirmed 403 Forbidden without one — we only hold CENSUS_API_KEY/FRED_API_KEY, neither applies). A national weekly Watermelon movement report (FVDTVMELON) exists keylessly too but showed no Florida row this week (September is off-season for FL watermelon, which peaks spring); citrus-specific Immokalee shipping-point reports were not located within budget. No prior brain-platform source overlaps this — it is genuinely new.

#### #93 citrus-stats (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: Confirmed live: USDA NASS's Florida field office (co-published with FDACS's Division of Fruit and Vegetables, Bartow FL) puts out free annual PDFs with county-level citrus acreage and production, and Collier and Hendry show up as first-class rows every year while Lee appears too but is small enough to sometimes get folded into an "Other Counties" bucket in production tables. This is a genuine rural-land-use series we don't hold: citrus acreage in Hendry/Collier has been collapsing hard (Collier 26,169 to 7,333 acres, Hendry 51,260 to 16,012 acres, both 2022 to 2025) which is exactly the kind of pre-development signal — grove abandonment/conversion years ahead of platting and permit filings — the operator is fishing for. FDACS's own citrus-statistics web page is a JS app that crawled empty; the real content lives on NASS's site as annual PDFs credited to both agencies. FDACS's separate GIS grove-polygon layer (if any) was not found within budget. Run 2: USDA NASS Florida Field Office (cooperating with FDACS — FDACS's own ag-statistics page names NASS's Florida office as "Florida Agricultural Statistics Service" and has no separate acreage dataset of its own) publishes an annual "Commercial Citrus Inventory" PDF with a county-by-year table of citrus acres AND 1,000-tree counts, covering Lee, Collier and Hendry every year back to 1996 (archive on the index page), most recently released 08/29/2025 for crop year 2025. Verified live: the 2024 report shows Collier 15,305 ac / Hendry 27,813 ac / Lee 1,055 ac (2024), and the 2025 report shows Collier 7,333 ac / Hendry 16,012 ac / Lee 799 ac (2025) — a roughly 50% one-year collapse in Collier and Lee acreage, consistent with HLB (citrus greening) disease attrition, not held anywhere in our stack today. A companion "Citrus Production Forecast" series exists (Oct/Jan/Apr/Jul releases per season) but is Florida-statewide only, no county breakout — useful context, not itself SWFL-grain. No API/keyless bulk endpoint exists for this series; it is PDF-only, table-shaped, one page per year.

#### #94 drought-fire (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: US Drought Monitor's keyless CountyStatistics API is fully live and verified for all three SWFL counties: weekly DSCI (drought severity composite index) back to 2000-01-04 for Hendry, and the finer 6-category (None/D0-D4) breakdown by FIPS. This is a clean, free, long-history, weekly leading-indicator candidate not currently held (we hold NOAA rainfall/storm events but nothing on soil-moisture-driven agricultural/water stress). FL Forest Service's public "Active Wildfires" ArcGIS FeatureServer is live and queryable by county (AdminDivision field) but is a real-time-only snapshot (4 statewide records at check time, none in Lee/Collier/Hendry) with no history endpoint found — low standalone value. The FDACS "Active Burn Authorizations" (OBA) ArcGIS service at gis.fdacs.gov returned a server-side 500 error consistently (dead end), and its historical "Burning Authorizations Summary" report at fireinfo.fdacs.gov is an ASP.NET WebForms postback report with no discoverable JSON/AJAX endpoint — scrape-shaped and out of budget for this pass (effort L, would need a headless browser). Run 2: Both named sources are real and live. The US Drought Monitor county-statistics API is a clean keyless CSV endpoint with weekly D0-D4 drought-category percentages for all three counties back to January 2000 — a strong, unheld, long-history leading-indicator candidate for agriculture/landscaping/water stress. The Florida Forest Service ArcGIS surfaces exist but are both snapshot-only (currently-active items, not an archive): a public "active burn authorizations" point layer (statewide 268 rows right now, one confirmed inside the Lee/Collier/Hendry bbox) and a public "active wildfire incidents" layer (4 rows statewide right now, none currently in Lee/Collier/Hendry, but the AdminDivision/county field supports filtering when fires do occur there). Neither wildfire/burn layer retains history — building a time series from them would require our own recurring poll, not a bulk pull.

#### #95 rural-lands (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: Verified two live, free ArcGIS REST feature services covering exactly this assignment. Collier's official RLSA_SRA_view layer gives the 11 approved Stewardship Receiving Area (SRA/future-town) polygons by name (Ave Maria, Bellmar Village, Rivergrass Village, Hyde Park Village, Brightshore Village, Big Cypress, Collier Rod and Gun Club) with acreage and a July 2022 vintage; its companion RLSA_SSA_ layer gives 28 Stewardship Sending Area (conservation-credit-generating) polygons. Lee County's SpecialPlanningArea layer (LeeCountyFLGIS org) captures the Density Reduction/Groundwater Resource (DR/GR) special planning boundaries — "Southeast Lee County" and "Bonita Springs DRGR" — as named polygons with goal/policy cross-references. Neither dataset carries a numeric stewardship-credit ledger or an explicit approval-workflow status field (pending vs. approved is not distinguished in the schema); that ledger appears to live only in Collier's PDF ordinances/staff reports, not as an open API or bulk file — flagged as a dead end, not confirmed absent. Run 2: Found and live-verified the authoritative Collier County RLSA GIS layers (Overlay boundary, approved Stewardship Receiving Areas/SRA "future towns", and Stewardship Sending Areas/SSA "credit source" parcels) hosted on ArcGIS Online by CollierCountyAGOL, and the actual Lee County Density Reduction/Groundwater Resource (DR/GR) Future Land Use Map category inside Lee's DCD_LeePlan MapServer (735 live polygons). None of these carry an approval-date, credit-count, or status field — they are boundary snapshots, not a pipeline tracker — so the real leading-indicator move is using these polygons as a spatial filter on data we already hold (Collier/Lee permits, deed records, parcels), not treating the layers themselves as an activity series. Longwater Village SRA, named in the assignment, was not found in the live SRA layer or in an ArcGIS Online search — not proof it doesn't exist, just not yet in this hosted view. A same-named "DRGR" feature service turned out to be an unrelated HUD Disaster-Recovery budget layer, a dead end worth flagging so nobody re-walks it.

ACS5 2024 is not yet released (204 empty as of this session); ACS5 2023 is the latest usable vintage and returns full tract-level rows for all three counties, including Hendry's small tracts and the water-only tract 9900 (nulls as -666666666). This is real incremental granularity beyond our existing 100 ZCTA rows: ACS5 tract gives ~224 tracts in Lee alone (vs ZCTA-level aggregation), covering B07 mobility/migration (in/out-of-county movers), B25 housing tenure/occupancy, B19 household income, and B25064 median gross rent, all sub-ZIP and available for Hendry (which has no ZCTA-level ACS1 presence at all since it's below the 20k population ACS1 threshold and small for ACS5 too but tracts still populate). Run 2: Verified live via api.census.gov with CENSUS_API_KEY: ACS 1-year 2024 is the latest county vintage (2025 not yet released, 404s) for Lee (12071) and Collier (12021) — both qualify for ACS1 since population exceeds the 65k threshold; Hendry (12051) returns HTTP 204 empty, confirming it's below the ACS1 threshold and only reachable via ACS5. ACS 5-year 2020-2024 (vintage "2024") tract data is live and covers all three counties: 223 tracts in Lee, 109 in Collier, 10 in Hendry (342 total tracts vs. the 100 ZCTA rows we currently hold — a real grain upgrade, tract is finer than ZCTA and unlocks migration/mobility tables ZCTA-level ACS5 doesn't reliably carry). Confirmed working variables: B25064 (median gross rent), B19013 (median household income), B25003 (owner/renter tenure), B07001 (geographic mobility/inflow — moved from different county or state, a literal in-migration count). #### #97 fhfa-uad (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: FHFA's UAD Aggregate Statistics Data File is free, bulk-CSV (zipped), no key needed, and does carry county-grain FIPS rows for Lee (12071), Collier (12021) and Hendry (12051) — verified live by grep on the downloaded county zips. The landing page text claims "Quarterly Data 2013Q1-2024Q3" for Enterprise SF, but the actual county-level v3_3 file (dated 12/18/2024) only carries data through 2023 for Lee/Collier (annual code Q5 included) — a real discrepancy between page copy and file content. The FHA Single-Family county file is annual-only at county grain (no quarterly breakout survived suppression for Lee/Collier), through 2023. Series cover appraised value (median, mean, quartiles), appraisal-vs-contract-price ratios, comps distance/adjustment, by PURPOSE (Purchase/Refinance/Both) — a genuine new field (loan purpose x appraisal value) not duplicated by FHFA HPI, which we already hold as a repeat-sales price index with no purpose split and no appraisal-vs-contract gap metric. Run 2: FHFA's UAD Aggregate Statistics is real, free, no-auth, live and distinct from the HPI we already hold: it publishes county-level (and national/state/CBSA/tract) aggregates of appraisal counts, median/mean appraised values, appraisal-vs-contract-price ratios, and comps characteristics, split by Enterprise Single-Family, Enterprise Condo, and FHA Single-Family, each by purchase/refi/both. Downloaded and grepped the actual county-level zipped CSVs (not just the landing page) and confirmed real rows for Lee County FL (FIPS 12071) and Collier County FL (FIPS 12021) in both the Enterprise-SF and FHA-SF county files, running quarterly from 2013 (Enterprise SF) / 2017 (FHA SF) through 2023 Q4 (the "2024 Q3" freshness claim on the landing page is for the national/all-geo file; county-level lags to 2023 Q4 as verified). The Enterprise Condo file only publishes down to CBSA level, not county, so it doesn't give SWFL rows. The most interesting series for a leading-indicator angle are Mean/Median Ratio of Appraised Value to Contract Price and % of Appraisals Below/Above/Equal to Contract Price - a widening gap (appraisals coming in under contract) is a straightforward pre-cursor to price softening or deal fall-throughs, ahead of closed-sale price data. Tract-level file exists too (untested here, same structure per data dictionary) for finer geography. Files are large (full county CSV ~1GB unzipped, ~28MB zipped) and update on an irregular/annual-ish cadence via manual FHFA releases, not a live API - effort is low to fetch, but data goes stale for ~9-12 months between refreshes.

#### #99 bls-ces-bed (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: CES (Current Employment Statistics) supersector payrolls ARE available live, keyless, at the exact MSA grain for both Cape Coral-Fort Myers (BLS area code 15980) and Naples-Marco Island (area code 34940), confirmed by fetching real August 2026 total-nonfarm values for both MSAs from the keyless BLS public API v1. This is genuinely not already held -- LAUS/QCEW/OEWS/PPI are different surveys -- and CES is a distinct monthly, establishment-based, supersector-split signal that can show sector rotation faster than QCEW's quarterly lag. BLS Business Employment Dynamics (gross job gains/losses) exists for Florida but only at the state level, no MSA/county breakout, so no added SWFL grain over what QCEW already gives. State JOLTS exists for Florida (confirmed via BLS's interactive state-JOLTS chart page) but I could not find the live series ID within budget, and it's state-grain only anyway so it would duplicate LAUS at a coarser level. download.bls.gov flat files and bls.gov/web/ bulk .txt tables both 403 curl (bot-blocked, exactly as warned) but crawl4ai renders them fine; the keyless api.bls.gov endpoint is the reliable machine-readable path for CES. Run 2: BLS's keyless public API v1 (api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v1/timeseries/data/{seriesID}) works without any key and returns real monthly CES employment for both Cape Coral-Fort Myers MSA (CBSA 15980) and Naples-Marco Island MSA (CBSA 34940), confirmed for total nonfarm and leisure/hospitality supersectors — this is a distinct, faster-cadence (monthly) series from our held LAUS/QCEW/OEWS/PPI. The catch: the keyless v1 tier ignores startyear/endyear and hard-caps history at ~2-3 years back regardless of range requested, so full historical backfill needs either BLS API v2 registration (a key we don't have) or the flat files, which are bot-blocked (403 on download.bls.gov). Florida-level JOLTS (job openings rate) is also live and keyless but state-grain only, no county/metro breakout exists at BLS — so it adds no SWFL-specific lead signal beyond what a national/state JOLTS series already implies. BLS Business Employment Dynamics (gross job gains/losses) is confirmed state-and-national grain only per BLS's own BDM landing page ("By States") — no metro/county series exists, so it's out of scope for SWFL-specific tracking.

#### #100 catalog-sweep (ran 2 times, merged)

Run 1: catalog.data.gov's CKAN API (/api/3/action/*) is fully dead — every path returns 404, including status_show, confirming this isn't a query-shape problem but the API itself being gone (likely retired in the 2025 GSA data.gov relaunch); the JS-rendered dataset search also ignores the ?q= param when crawled, so no path into that catalog exists right now. FGDL (Florida Geographic Data Library) is alive and huge — 592 statewide layers in its interactive catalog — but nearly all are environmental/regulatory point layers (brownfields, hazardous waste, cleanup sites) that are new to our holdings even though they sit adjacent to the "permits/property" theme rather than squarely outside it. The one I verified live and county-filterable is FDEP's petroleum-contamination-site cleanup tracker: 952 Lee, 474 Collier, 110 Hendry records with a cleanup-status field (site closure = land freed for redevelopment), a genuine and not-yet-covered lead signal. geodata.floridagio.gov is an ArcGIS Hub; its org-scoped ArcGIS search (orgid Gh9awoU677aKree0) returned zero hits for opportunity zones, CRAs, broadband, enterprise zones, vacant land, foreclosure, and rural-area-of-opportunity layers — either FGIO doesn't host them or they're indexed under different exact titles I didn't guess; Lee-County-tagged results there were limited to the statewide parcel layer we already hold. FGDL's own catalog search box does not accept URL query params (Oracle APEX interactive grid, JS-driven), so I could not keyword-filter its 592-row list within budget; a full manual page-by-page read of all 46 pages was out of scope for this pass. Run 2: catalog.data.gov's classic CKAN action API (package_search) is dead — every call returned an app-level 404 "Not Found", and the public search UI at catalog.data.gov/dataset ignores the ?q= parameter entirely (returns the same generic "most popular" list regardless of query), so that catalog could not be searched live in this session. FGDL (fgdl.org) is alive with 592 current layers across a browsable ORDS catalog; geodata.floridagio.gov exposes a working ArcGIS Hub search API (/api/search/v1/collections/dataset/items) that resolves to live ArcGIS FeatureServer/MapServer endpoints. The most promising completeness-sweep finds are FDEP environmental contamination/cleanup and permit layers served through a single UF GeoPlan ArcGIS REST service (FDEP_Waste_Groups) — petroleum-discharge cleanup status, brownfield redevelopment areas, and large-construction NPDES stormwater permits — plus a stale-but-unique 2009/2014 SFWMD saltwater-intrusion (isochlor/chloride) layer and a thin statewide sinkhole (subsidence) point layer. Row counts for Lee/Collier/Hendry on most of these are small (single digits to low hundreds), so this sweep surfaced niche, not blockbuster, additions — the two catalogs' own search tooling is the bigger finding.
